title: BPO Property Record
description: Canonical record for a single blockchain-assurance property in the Blockchain Property Ontology (BPO). One file == one property. Designed to be simultaneously human-authored, machine-validated (this schema), and RDF-projectable (see context.jsonld). Required fields are deliberately a small core so the living database can grow incrementally; everything else is schema-defined but optional, to be populated as a property matures from `draft` to `stable`.

id.description: Opaque, immutable canonical identifier. Semantically meaningless by design (cf. CWE-NNN, Wikidata Q-numbers): reclassification must never force an ID change. Never reuse a retired ID.

slug.description: Human-readable stable handle. May be revised; `id` is the join key.

version.description: SemVer of this record. MAJOR = semantics of the property changed (breaks downstream proofs); MINOR = facets added; PATCH = editorial.

external_refs.description: Cross-walk to existing registries so BPO sits *beside* CWE/SWC/DASP/DASCP rather than re-inventing them.

dascp.description: Cross-walk to the DASCP framework (DTCC/Clearstream/Euroclear, 2024). Each entry references a DASCP principle (Pn), risk (Rn), or control (Cnn-{L,S,R,N}). The `relation` qualifier distinguishes `establishes` (the BPO property mechanically discharges this DASCP control), `supports` (the BPO property materially contributes), and `partially-supports` (the BPO property covers one facet of a multi-facet control). DASCP ids resolve against mappings/dascp.framework.json; closure is enforced by schema/validate_refs.py the same way BPO: edges are.

iso20022.description: Depth-1 cross-walk to the ISO 20022 financial-messaging standard (property ↔ message / business component / data element). Each entry references an ISO 20022 id resolved against mappings/iso20022.framework.json. `relates-to` indicates general relevance; `constrains` indicates the property places a behavioural constraint on operations of this message/component type. Closure is enforced by schema/validate_refs.py the same way DASCP cross-walks are.

classification.description: Faceted, orthogonal classification. A property is a POINT in this space, not a leaf in a single tree. Axes are independent; each may carry multiple values (a property can be both safety w.r.t. one trace set and a 2-safety hyperproperty).

modal_class.description: Alpern-Schneider trace-property class, extended with Clarkson-Schneider hyperproperties. Critical distinction: privacy/ZK/MEV/fairness properties are HYPERproperties (relate multiple traces) and are NOT verifiable by single-trace reachability tools.

deontic_role.description: Assume/guarantee + deontic role. An `assumption` is something the property RELIES ON (and must be discharged elsewhere); a `guarantee` is what it OFFERS. Mislabeling here is the most common source of unsound composition.

domains.description: SKOS concept slugs from ontology/taxonomy (poly-hierarchy). e.g. 'evm', 'zk-circuit', 'defi-lending', 'cross-chain', 'agentic'.

decidability.description: Honest statement of what is mechanically achievable. Many liveness and all cryptographic-indistinguishability properties are not decidable by automated tools and require ITP or pen-and-paper reduction.

system_theoretic.description: Facet 3: property as a constraint on a transition system / control system.

execution_semantics.description: Facet 5: how it manifests in concrete execution / where violations live.

formalization.description: Facet 2 + 16-19. Multiple logics intentionally; a property is over-determined so downstream tools can pick their native encoding. Strings are LaTeX-ish / tool-syntax; not executed by this schema.

signature.description: State vocabulary: sorts, functions, predicates the formulae range over. The canonical declaration site for symbols the property quantifies over; depth-2 ISO 20022 bindings whose property has no `symbols` list fall back to a whole-token regex match against this field.

symbols.description: Optional declarative list of named symbols (sorts, functions, predicates, transition labels) the formalization quantifies over. When present, depth-2 ISO 20022 bindings must reference symbols from this list as exact case-sensitive matches (the structured, trustworthy path). When absent, schema/validate_refs.py falls back to a whole-token regex match against `signature` — case-sensitive, no near-match.

fairness.description: Fairness assumptions REQUIRED for any liveness claim to hold; omitting these is a soundness bug.

hyperproperty.description: Relational/2-safety/simulator formulation when modal_class includes a hyperproperty.

bindings.description: Depth-2 ISO 20022 binding: each entry maps a formalization symbol to an ISO 20022 element / component / message. The bound `element` must resolve in mappings/iso20022.framework.json; the bound `symbol` must satisfy the symbol-in-formalization check — structured lookup against `formalization.symbols` when present, else whole-token regex against `formalization.signature`. Both checks are enforced by schema/validate_refs.py. A binding that silently mis-resolves would be worse than no binding, so the check is strict and case-sensitive.

relationships.description: Facet 8. Typed edges forming a poly-hierarchical DAG (NOT a tree). Edge semantics defined in schema/relationship.vocab.json.

target.description: BPO id, or attack-class id for `mitigates`.

incident_refs.description: Curated, must be verified before status>=reviewed; provenance.confidence flags unverified.

assumptions.description: First-class discharge ledger: every environmental/trust/cryptographic assumption the guarantee rests on. A guarantee is only as strong as its undischarged assumptions; making these explicit is the whole point of assume-guarantee reasoning.

discharged_by.description: BPO id or external proof artifact discharging it. `null` is meaningful: an explicitly accepted but UNDISCHARGED assumption — these are exactly what an assurance review must surface.
